# ADR-0008: Persistent chunks in Feed, as a rebuildable BM25 index

## Status

Accepted (2026-07-10, not yet implemented).

## Decision

Chunking moves out of the downstream Dossier-owned extract path into Feed as persistent, queryable rows: span chunks over an article revision's immutable text, and one chunk per Live update. The whole chunk layer (rows plus FTS index) is a rebuildable derived artifact: destroyable and rebuilt from `articles` and `live_posts` by one command, which is safe only because chunk refs are deterministic (ADR-0004). Retrieval is staged and lexical-first: chunk-grain BM25 now, then article-grain plus chunk-grain rank fusion (RRF), with a per-hit ranking feature log (query, refs, per-stage ranks and scores, weights, filters, chunker tag) on every response. The chunk index is an external-content FTS5 table using `porter unicode61 remove_diacritics 2`, a deliberate divergence from the unstemmed article index, because consumer questions are natural language and recall-oriented.

## Considered options

- Keep chunking downstream (the Dossier-owned extract path): rejected, chunks were transient in-memory objects, so nothing could cite, re-read, or benchmark them.
- Contentful FTS (the `articles_search` pattern): rejected for chunks, it stores the corpus twice.

## Consequences

- Any chunker change (constants, boundary rules, normalization) means a full re-chunk; mixed chunker generations in one table are forbidden.
- Each chunk row carries a text hash plus a short quote prefix/su

# ADR-0004: One opaque article ref; deterministic chunk refs

## Status

Accepted (2026-07-10, not yet implemented).

## Decision

An article has exactly one public identity: `art-<yyyymmdd>-<hex8>` (acquisition date plus 8 random hex characters, the repo's run-id style), minted once by Feed at first acquisition and carrying no publisher, title, or URL semantics. Chunk refs derive from it deterministically: `<article_ref>#r<revision>:<start>-<end>` for span chunks (half-open character offsets in UTF-16 code units into that revision's stored body) and `<article_ref>#p:<post_id>` for live-update chunks. Identity lives in the ref; everything informative (title, publisher, URL, dates, hashes) lives in response fields. Only Feed mints refs: consumers deriving their own identities for feed content (as the pipeline adapter did with a projection hash) is banned. `url_hash`, `content_hash`, and `title_hash` remain internal dedup attributes and never cross the boundary.

## Considered options

- Promote the legible file ids (`art-<date>-<site>-<slug>`) to public refs: rejected. Embedded site/date/title invite parsing (Hyrum's law) and become lies after alias flips (ADR-0006) or upstream corrections; the current minting also has a live collision defect (the filename gets a dedup counter, the id does not; 13 shared-id pairs exist across the 21,138 article rows as of 2026-07-10).
- Typed-prefix ULIDs: rejected. Monotonicity at scale is a property we do not need, and it breaks the repo's legible date+hex token style.

## Consequences

- Deterministic chunk-ref derivation is what lets the chunk layer stay a rebuildable index (ADR-0008) without breaking refs anyone holds.
- The span unit (UTF-16 code units) is part of the public contract and needs a non-ASCII fixture test.
- Backfill mints refs for every existing article; old file ids remain as file names only.

# ADR-0009: Feed retrieval never triggers acquisition; responses carry coverage

## Status

Accepted (2026-07-10, not yet implemented).

## Decision

Every Feed read (search, deref) is a pure read: it never scans, fetches, or blocks on a Provider. This deliberately deviates from Vendor's fetch-on-demand default (vendor ADR-0004) because Feed acquisition is browser-driven, minutes-slow, login-stateful, and quota-bound, none of which belongs inside a query path. Scans stay scheduled; the only demand-driven acquisition is the repair queue and the manual refresh command (ADR-0005). Because "no results" is ambiguous in a pull-based corpus, every search response carries coverage metadata (which Providers were scanned for the queried window, and when, from `source_scans`) so a consumer can distinguish "nothing published" from "not scanned yet" and request a scan out of band.

## Considered options

- Synchronous fetch-on-demand like Vendor: rejected, minutes-long latency and a logged-in browser dependency inside the retrieval path, with quota burn driven by query patterns instead of a schedule.
- Async scan-request queue: deferred until a real consumer proves the need.

### T5: Persistent chunks + one-command rebuild

Status: done.

Implements ADR-0008's storage half. `src/db.ts`: guarded migration `ensureChunkSchema()` (CREATE TABLE/VIRTUAL
TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, same no-op-on-existing-store style as `ensureArticleRevisionSchema`, no ALTER needed
since these are new tables) adds `chunks` (chunk_ref TEXT PRIMARY KEY, article_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES
articles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, kind, revision, char_start, char_end, post_id, chunk_index, chunker_ver, text,
text_sha256, quote_prefix/suffix, denormalized published_at/site/section/type) plus an index on article_id, and
`chunks_fts` (external-content FTS5, `tokenize='porter unicode61 remove_diacritics 2'`, the stemmed divergence
from `articles_search`) with the three sync triggers (delete form re-supplies old rowid/text, matching the
existing `articles_search`/`live_posts_search` trigger shape). Also caches once per open whether
`articles.duplicate_of` exists (ADR-0006, not implemented anywhere in this codebase yet): a non-NULL
`duplicate_of` on a row skips chunking once that column exists; every row is canonical until then, per the
ticket's explicit instruction.

`src/chunks/build.ts` (new, pure functions, no DB access): `buildSpanChunks` runs `chunkText` (PF-2's chunker)
over an article's CURRENT body, mints `<article_ref>#r<revision>:<charStart>-<charEnd>` per chunk via
`spanChunkRef`, and sets `quote_prefix`/`quote_suffix` to up to 32 UTF-16 units before/after the span, clamped
to the body's own bounds (0 prefix at the start, 0 suffix at the end). `buildLivePostChunks` builds one chunk
per `live_posts` row, ref `<article_ref>#p:<post_id>` via `livePostChunkRef`, `kind: 'live-post'`, `chunk_index`
= the post's `position`, `revision`/`char_start`/`char_end` null (no shared-body span concept for a live post),
`quote_prefix`/`quote_suffix` empty (schema default, nothing meaningful to derive them from).

# Feed Source Service

The acquisition and retrieval half of the system's feed capability. It scrapes a fixed set of Providers for articles and live-blog updates, persists them, and serves them to consumers through `feedq`. It is the source of truth for acquired feed source material and its retrieval indexes, and for nothing else: notes, truth, verification, vendor facts, roster relevance, and memory live in other contexts. LLM-driven work of any kind (extraction, classification, validation, clustering, synthesis, enrichment) is out of scope here. The identity, revision, and chunk vocabulary below is decided language (ADR-0004 through ADR-0010, accepted 2026-07-10) that implementation is still catching up to: today `feedq` serves article-grain BM25 and still prints internal ids.

In documents this context is called the Feed Source Service (or Feed Source Retrieval).
_Avoid_: Feed and Analytics.

## Language

### Acquisition

**Provider**:
The adapter for one of the nine supported feed publishers (Wireone, WIRETWO, WIRETHREE, WIREFOUR, Portalone Vendor, Assistantone, Wireseven, WIREEIGHT, Wiresix): it lists a publisher's articles and extracts their content, optionally including live blogs.
_Avoid_: source, feed, site, publisher (publisher means the human-facing organization; Provider means the adapter).

**Scan**:
One end-to-end acquisition run over a date range. A Scan visits each selected Provider's listings, collects article links, extracts content for new links, discovers Live updates, and (once ADR-0005 lands) drains the Repair queue. A Scan is the unit of idempotency: re-running over the same range re-checks but does not re-extract unchanged articles.
_Avoid_: crawl, fetch run, ingest.

**Article**:
One acquired piece of feed content (title, summary, clean body text, publication metadata). Publicly identified by its Article ref; its text advances through Revisions. The internal `content_hash` (SHA-256 of the first 2,000 characters of the cleaned body; absent for very sho
